item.title: City of Shawnee Wards 1, 5 and 6 up for election in June
item.description: Shawnee residents should be on the lookout for candidate listings in April, as those interested could be filing to serve on the city commission.

item.title: Orange Barrel Alert: Road closure on Garrett's Lake Road
item.description: Pottawatomie County District 1 reports that Garrett's Lake Road is being impacted by a road closure through early next week. Garretts Lake Road, between Bryan and Brangus Road, was shut down Thursday morning and will remain closed in this section through 7 a.m.

item.title: Rising Star Gymnastics trio excels at Bart Conner Invitational
item.description: NORMAN – Three boys from Shawnee’s Rising Star Gymnastics – Jackson Bottoms, Luke Mailloux and Otavio Volpe - recently excelled at the Bart Conner Invitational.

item.title: Gardens of the Cross Timbers: Happy Heart Day
item.description: Just about to start this article on Valentine’s Day when the siren blared in my driveway from the vehicle with flashing lights. The officer came to my door.

item.title: Beyond Reason: My sweetheart
item.description: Valentine’s Day didn’t begin as a celebration of your loved one. February 14 started out as a church feast day honoring Saint Valentine, which was not especially romantic.

item.title: Isaiah Wade re-signs with Potawatomi Fire for 2026
item.description: The Potawatomi Fire are excited to announce the re-signing of Isaiah Wade for the 2026 TBL season. Wade (6-7, forward) will be playing in his third consecutive season with the Fire, after helping the Fire win TBL titles in 2024 and 2025.

item.title: SSC professor releases sixth book
item.description: Seminole State College Assistant Professor of English Paul Juhasz has released his sixth book, Katabasis, a new collection of poems published by Turning Plow Press. In Katabasis, Juhasz explores grief, memory and the complicated work of recovery, using the ancient idea of a descent “into the world below” as a lens for modern life.

item.title: Outdoor class part of THS forensic criminology program
item.description: Tecumseh High School students stepped outside the classroom earlier this week for a hands-on lab as part of the district's new Forensic Criminology program. This course, taught by retired Tecumseh Police Officer Billy Crow, is already making a big impact.
